description: Solo team. A graphic and product designer working on the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Not looking for new members.
summary: NASA Robot Cards is an interactive web collection of holographic digital trading cards about real NASA robots that stopped working and stayed on Mars, the Moon or in deep space. It is made for school-age kids and casual space fans. Series 1 includes two finished cards, the Opportunity rover and the Ingenuity helicopter, plus a locked "Coming soon" card for Pioneer 10. Tap a card and the robot's real NASA 3D model stands up on it. Kids can explore its parts, open its achievements and read its story in three short chapters. Part popovers, achievement stories and chapters link to NASA sources. The goal: turn dense mission pages into robot legends kids want to collect, explore and remember.
details:
What it does

NASA Robot Cards is a web collection of holographic digital trading cards featuring real NASA robots that finished their missions and remain on Mars, the Moon or in deep space. Series 1 has two complete cards, the Opportunity Mars rover and the Ingenuity Mars helicopter, and a locked "Coming soon" card for the Pioneer 10 deep-space probe.

How it works

Tap a card: it lies flat and the robot's real NASA 3D model stands up on it. You can rotate the model and tap labeled parts, such as Opportunity's camera mast, solar panels and wheels, or Ingenuity's rotor blades, solar panel and legs, to learn what each part does. A side panel shows achievements with short "Learn more" stories, a three-chapter story with star progress, a map (Opportunity's historical route map, or an approximate Jezero Crater location for Ingenuity), and a mission log. Text is short, key achievements use icons, numbers and short labels, and part popovers, achievement stories and chapters link to NASA sources.

Why it matters

The challenge brief notes that school-age space enthusiasts often hear only about active, ongoing missions. The robots that stopped working have amazing stories that are buried in dense technical pages. Opportunity was planned to work for about 3 months after landing on Jan. 24, 2004, yet kept exploring for more than 14 years, drove 45.16 km (the first marathon distance on another world) and found hematite "blueberries" that usually form in water, until a planet-wide dust storm silenced it on June 10, 2018. The 1.8 kg Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet on April 19, 2021, and flew 72 times instead of the planned 5.

What I hope to achieve

I want kids to feel that these robots are real heroes, and to make their stories easy and exciting to collect, explore and remember. Next steps: new series with robots left on the Moon and Pioneer 10 in deep space, and cards that kids unlock by finishing short mini-missions.

Tools used

Designed in Figma and Photoshop. Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using Google model-viewer 4.4.0 for the 3D models, hosted on Cloudflare. The code was written with Codex (an AI coding tool) from my instructions, and the holographic card background art was generated with Figma AI and edited by me; it is marked "AI-generated background" on the site.
